title: Zululand
capsule: Zululand denotes the territory of the independent Zulu Kingdom, founded by Shaka ka Senzangakhona around 1816 through the consolidation of Nguni clans by military innovation including the short stabbing assegai and the age-regiment system. Under Cetshwayo kaMpande, the kingdom inflicted a catastrophic defeat on British forces at Isandlwana on 22 January 1879, the worst British defeat by an African army in the colonial era, before being broken at Ulundi in July 1879. Britain formally annexed Zululand in 1887 and incorporated it into the Colony of Natal in 1897, ending the kingdom's political independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's territorial extent is well documented through British colonial surveys and contemporary maps, especially for the 1879 war period; earlier expansionary boundaries under Shaka are reconstructed from oral tradition and traveller accounts.
